sub_answers.text: From 1974 county-level functions for Newcastle were provided by Tyne and Wear County Council while district councils provided district-level functions [d41381311s0p0][d67582869s1p0]. When Tyne and Wear County Council was abolished in 1986 its functions passed to the area’s district councils, making those councils responsible for both district- and county-level functions, sometimes delivered via joint arrangements with other Tyne and Wear councils [d41381311s0p0][d41381311s2p0]. Regional combined authorities have since been created that interact with the city: the North of Tyne Combined Authority (created 2018) with an elected mayor from 2019, and a wider North East Mayoral Combined Authority established in 2024 chaired by a directly elected regional mayor to oversee strategic functions across the area including Newcastle [d67582869s1p0][d41381311s2p0].
